newsitem.title: JAPAN: EMU convergence criteria may not be sufficient - BOE.
newsitem.headline: EMU convergence criteria may not be sufficient - BOE.

text.p: Conditions set by convergence criteria may not be fully sufficient for successful European economic and monetary union (EMU), Howard Davies, deputy governor of the Bank of England, said on Wednesday.

"There are good grounds for believing that the convergence criteria are not a sufficient condition for safe membership of EMU," Davies said in a speech to the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan in Tokyo.
Davies said a country considering membership should be satisfied that it can perform against the criteria on a sustained basis, not just in one benchmark year.
"Improvements in public-sector deficit ratios, resulting from unrepeatable one-off measures, will not produce sustainable fiscal consolidation," he said.
He said there were considerable market doubts about the ability of some countries to meet the criteria.

"You can see evidence of that uncertainty in the market price of bonds and options. Italian and Spanish bond yields have moved closer to German bunds in the last year but they remain some distance apart," he said.
Davies also said he saw a "wide and deep euro-denominated debt market, quite soon after 1999" if EMU went ahead on time.
"Governments in euro countries will issue new debt denominated in euros and convert existing debt into euros. I imagine that many companies will also begin to do so, very quickly," he said.
Davies also said London would be a strong financial centre even if Britain was not among the first wave of EMU members.

"Our work on preparing the City of London for EMU convinces us that the City, as a financial marketplace, will be as well-prepared as any for EMU when the time comes, and better prepared than most," he said.

He added that while it had been argued that London might not have full access to Europe's payment systems through the TARGET mechanism, the BOE did not regard that lack of full access as a serious competitive threat.
TARGET will link the real-time settlement systems of different member countries.
Davies said the United Kingdom would be linked to TARGET and that the only serious question would be the extent to which intra-day credit would be available to those outside the euro-zone.
He added that the BOE was examining all alternative possibilities for making euro payments in Britain.
